newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan newspaper contests defamation verdict.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan newspaper contests defamation verdict.

text.p: The Kenyan newspaper The People owned by an oppositon leader appealed on Tuesday against a high court verdict that it had defamed a personal aide of President Daniel arap Moi.

High Court Judge Emmanuel O'Kubasu last week awarded 10 million Kenyan shillings ($183,500) to Joshuah Kulei after finding that the weekly newspaper had defamed him. He said the verdict was based on The People failing to enter a defence.
O'Kubasu's award was the highest for demafation or libel in Kenya's history and sent shivers through the Kenyan media ahead of presidential and parliamentary elections later this year.
On Monday lawyer James Orengo for The People said the 10 million shillings in damages was excessive under Kenyan law and argued that such awards only ranged between 400,000 and a million shillings.

The People, owned by opposition leader Kenneth Matiba, said in January Kulei, an aide to Moi for 18 years, was linked to businessmen of Asian origin who used political partronage to win contracts and were involved in corrupt deals.
Kulei said The People had portrayed him as dishonest and corrupt.
On Tuesday, Orengo lodged his appeal before Judge O'Kubasu and argued that The People had in fact entered a defence but the high court had either not seen the documents or ignored them.
Hearing dates for the appeal were not immediately known.
Kulei's lawyers told the judge they would hold their claim to the 10 million shillings until The People's appeal was heard and determined. They said they believed in a fair hearing.
The People says it is editorially independent despite being owned by Matiba.

It has emerged as a leading alternative voice in a country where television and radio stations are owned by people with close links to ruling politicians. Magazines and newspapers have mixed ownership. ($1=54.50 Kenyan shillings)
